t: 3772. Maximum Subgraph Score in a Tree
o: Assign each node weight +1 (good) or -1 (bad); for every node find the maximum total weight of a connected subgraph containing it. In a tree, connected subgraphs containing v correspond to choosing, for each neighbor direction, either nothing or a connected piece hanging that way, and only pieces with positive total weight are worth taking. Example 2: node 1 collects its good children 3 and 4 (score 3), while bad node 0 attaches to node 1's positive component for score 2. This is the classic two-pass rerooting DP: g[v] = best score using v's subtree, then propagate parent-side gains downward.
k: Down pass: g[v] = w[v] + sum of max(0, g[child]) over children - only positive child components are attached.
Reroot pass: up[c] = max(0, g[parent] + up[parent] - max(0, g[c])) captures the best gain obtainable through the parent side.
Answer for every node is ans[v] = g[v] + up[v].
Use an iterative BFS-order traversal to avoid recursion-depth failures at n = 1e5.

a.i: Root the tree at 0, compute g bottom-up, then answer top-down by passing each child the parent-side surplus (everything the parent can offer besides the child's own subtree, clamped at 0). Short and elegant; raise the recursion limit in Python.
s: Build adjacency; DFS from root computing g[v] = w[v] + sum(max(0, g[child])).
For each child c of v: up[c] = max(0, g[v] + up[v] - max(0, g[c])); ans[c] = g[c] + up[c]; recurse.
a.t: O(n) - each node and edge is visited a constant number of times across the two DFS passes
a.sp: O(n) for adjacency, g, up, and recursion stack

a.n: Approach 2: Iterative BFS-order rerooting (safe for deep trees)
a.i: Replace recursion with an explicit BFS to get a parent array and traversal order; process the order backwards for the down pass and forwards for the up pass. Identical recurrences, no stack-overflow risk.
s: BFS from node 0 recording parent[] and order[].
Reverse order: g[u] += max(0, g[child]) accumulated into parents.
Forward order: up[u] = max(0, g[p] + up[p] - max(0, g[u])); ans[u] = g[u] + up[u].
a.t: O(n) - constant work per node in each of the three linear passes
a.sp: O(n) for adjacency, parent array, order, and DP arrays

w: Always present rerooting as 'down pass + up pass'; draw example 2 to justify the max(0, ...) clamps. Pitfalls: recursing in Python at n = 1e5 (use the iterative version), forgetting the clamp when the parent side is net-negative, and rooting assumptions (any root works). Follow-up: return the actual node set, or handle edge weights / node updates.
